messages.author: 54f369bce6d6a87f
messages.subject: Repeated server disconnects
parts:
I have the development version of an app in my personal (free) Shinyapps account, and the production version in a paid account. As of today, any attempt to use the dev version results, fairly quickly, in a server disconnect. The dev version works fine on my local machine, and the production version continues to run fine on the Shinyapps server.

Among other things. I tried rolling the dev version back to the commit that matches the production version, then republishing it to my account. That version also dies with a server disconnect. The code should be identical to the (correctly working) production version, but the supporting package versions will be more recent. That would lead me to suspect some problem introduced by a package update, but the server logs tell me nothing. I'm attaching a log showing everything from the dev server restart to the first disconnect. All it has is the usual harmless warnings.

The dev version does not die instantly. It lets me upload a spreadsheet file and view the data in a DT. As soon as I specify the variables for a regression, though, it's toast.

It's not a memory problem (according to my dashboard, it maxes out below 50 MB), or a timeout problem. I would greatly appreciate any help debugging this.

TIA,
Paul

messages.author: 54f369bce6d6a87f
messages.subject: Re: Repeated server disconnects
parts:
On Wednesday, June 7, 2017 at 7:01:42 PM UTC-4, Joshua Spiewak wrote:
Could you share the application's URL?

Sure. It's https://parubin.shinyapps.io/scm871/. You'll need a data set in a .xlsx file to test it. I've been using a couple of the data sets that come with R, including the Duncan employment data (4.8 KB Excel file). All the app does (when it works) is plot individual variables, let the user run a linear regression, and then provide some diagnostic plots and tests.

In the first tab, upper left in the left panel, there's a button to upload your data. There are controls to pin down where in the Excel file the data is, but if your data is in the first tab with nothing other than maybe empty cells above it, you should be able to skip them. Once the data has been inhaled, there's a tab with a DT showing the data. That does not seem to be a crash source. I can sort columns and such without a server disconnect.

The next tab lets you plot one variable, and optionally plot the interaction of two variables, and the tab after that lets you specify a linear model. When I do anything with either of those tabs, the server usually disconnects immediately. I've had a couple of instances where I could plot one variable okay, but whatever I did next triggered the disconnect. Other times, even plotting one variable blows it up.

Just to repeat, the same application code is running in a paid account with no problems, and the dev version was running fine until a day or so ago. The only thing I can think of that might have changed in the dev version was the versions of the supporting libraries.

Thanks for responding.

Paul
